title: SYSK Selects: How Black Friday Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the classic episode on Black Friday. Josh and Chuck explain the day after Thanksgiving as the start of the US holiday shopping season, trace the term's origin to 1960s Philadelphia police, bus drivers and cab drivers (not the 'in the black' accounting myth), and cover how retailers created Cyber Monday (2005) and Small Business Saturday (2010), and pushed sales into Thanksgiving. They discuss doorbuster deals as bait-and-switch, violent Black Friday incidents including the 2008 Valley Stream, Long Island Walmart stampede that killed employee Jdimytai Damour (spelled Jim Tad More in transcript), the 2008 Palm Desert Toys R Us shooting, and a 2011 Los Angeles Walmart pepper spray incident, plus the Buy Nothing Day counter-movement and China's Singles Day shopping event.
topics: Toys R Us Palm Desert shooting

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday framing
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects rerun and the hosts banter about Black Friday sales, with Chuck saying he has never been to one and both expressing dislike of the crowds, while acknowledging others enjoy them.

segments.title: What Black Friday is and its early roots
segments.summary: The day after Thanksgiving is described as the busiest US shopping day. The hosts trace the idea of starting holiday shopping to late-19th/early-20th-century department store Thanksgiving parades featuring Santa Claus, and discuss Macy's parade.

segments.title: Philadelphia origin of the term Black Friday
segments.summary: The term is traced to 1960s Philadelphia, where police, bus drivers and city workers called the day Black Friday because out-of-towners came for the Army-Navy game and crowded downtown sales. Retailers later promoted a different origin. The accounting 'in the black' myth is debunked.

segments.title: Retail stakes and the holiday spending boom
segments.summary: Stores earn a large share of retail profits in the holiday season, and the National Retail Federation projected about $682 billion spent in November and December 2013. The hosts discuss personal gift-giving habits.

segments.title: Black Friday as a manufactured tradition; Cyber Monday and Small Business Saturday
segments.summary: Retailers promoted Black Friday as the busiest shopping day starting around 2004, replacing the Saturday before Christmas. Cyber Monday (2005) and American Express's Small Business Saturday (2010) followed as self-fulfilling retail inventions.

segments.title: Stores opening on Thanksgiving and shortened season
segments.summary: Retailers including Walmart in 2012, Kmart, Macy's and others began opening on Thanksgiving, which the hosts see as eroding the holiday. Because Thanksgiving fell late in 2013, retailers had a shorter season, and Black Friday may hurt sales compared to countries without it.

segments.title: Doorbusters, bait-and-switch and shopper statistics
segments.summary: Doorbuster deals on a few limited items are described as bait-and-switch tactics that lure shoppers in. The hosts cite survey numbers on shoppers, average shopping time, and the growing role of online shopping.

segments.title: Message break
segments.summary: A short break in the episode.

segments.title: 2008 Valley Stream Walmart stampede
segments.summary: At a Valley Stream, Long Island Walmart, a crowd of about 2,000 waiting for Black Friday doors broke barricades and crushed shoppers. Employee Jdimytai Damour was trampled and died, and pregnant shopper Leanna Lockley was pulled inside. Police had left, and security was minimal. The hosts describe other trampling videos and the lack of legal bans.

segments.title: Other Black Friday violence and Buy Nothing Day
segments.summary: The hosts recount the 2008 Palm Desert, California Toys R Us shooting between two husbands after a fight between wives, and a 2011 Los Angeles Walmart pepper spray incident. They also describe Buy Nothing Day, started by Ted Dave and promoted by Adbusters, plus protest costumes and Singles Day in China.
topics: Toys R Us Palm Desert shooting

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wish listeners a happy Thanksgiving, urge civility on Black Friday, and sign off with show contact info.
